# Flashcard Infographic — Design

**Goal:** Let a deck's flashcards be turned into a one-page infographic — a title plus a handful of icon-and-bullet sections summarizing the material — generated by the same Claude integration this app already uses to draft cards and write test questions. Reachable from Deck Manager once the deck has cards.

**Scope in one line:** one infographic per deck, generated on demand from either every card or a chosen subset, rendered through a layout this app owns and controls — not arbitrary HTML the model writes.

## Decisions (all confirmed 2026-09-13)

| Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| How the model's output becomes the visual | The model returns **structured JSON** (a title, 3–6 sections, each an icon + heading + 2–5 bullet points); the app renders it through **one fixed layout/CSS we design**, never the model's own markup | This app has never rendered arbitrary HTML from anywhere (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no iframe) — every AI response so far is structured JSON a typed component renders (cards, quiz questions). Letting the model emit real HTML/CSS would need iframe sandboxing and would make every deck's infographic look inconsistent. Structured data keeps this feature on the same footing as everything else the app already does with a model response. |
| Icon choice | The model picks from a **fixed enum** of icon names given to it in the prompt; nothing freeform | The app can only render icons it has SVGs for. A closed vocabulary means there is never an icon name that has to fall back silently. |
| Where the infographic is shown | A **dedicated route**, `/deck/:id/infographic`, phase-driven like `/deck/:id/test` (`TestMode`'s `setup → generating → taking → results`, here `setup → generating → view`) | Consistent with Study and Test already being their own screens rather than modals; an infographic benefits from full-screen room the way a test does. |
| Which cards feed it | Either **every card**, or a **chosen subset** picked from a checklist before generating | The user's own call: default to simplicity (all cards) but don't force it — a large or mixed deck may only want its core cards represented. |
| Storage | **A new `infographics` IndexedDB store**, `keyPath: 'deckId'` (one row per deck, `DB_VERSION` 3→4) — not a field on the `Deck` record | Mirrors why `flashcards` and `testQuestions` already live in their own stores: `getAllDecks()` is read every time the library opens, and it shouldn't get heavier because decks can now have infographics. |
| Regenerating | **Overwrites** the stored infographic. No version history | Matches how card drafting already works — generation is "kept until you replace it," not versioned. Smallest thing that could work; versioning is a clear, callable-out future addition, not a silent gap. |
| AI gating | Same `AiSettings` (`off` / `hosted` / `byok`) already used for cards and quiz — the setup screen shows the same "turn on the AI helper" panel when it's off | One AI on/off switch for the whole app, not a second one for this feature. |
| Cost confirmation | **None** beyond the "Generate infographic" button itself | Matches "Write missing questions" and card drafting: an explicit button press is already the confirmation; no extra "are you sure" dialog. |
| Export / download | **Out of scope for v1** | Flagged as a deliberate cut so it reads as a choice, not an oversight — a clear, small follow-up once the core feature ships. |

## Data model

`src/types.ts` — three new exports, alongside the existing `Deck`/`Folder`/`Flashcard`:

```ts
/**
 * The icons an infographic section can carry. Fixed on purpose: the app can
 * only render icons it ships its own SVG for, so the model is given exactly
 * this list in the prompt and never asked to invent a name.
 */
export type InfographicIcon =
  | 'book' | 'lightbulb' | 'brain' | 'chart' | 'list'
  | 'arrows' | 'target' | 'clock' | 'check' | 'warning'
  | 'network' | 'question';

export interface InfographicSection {
  heading: string;
  icon: InfographicIcon;
  /** 2–5 short bullet points, clamped on parse — see parseInfographicResponse. */
  points: string[];
}

/**
 * One deck's infographic. Regenerating replaces this record outright; there
 * is no history of earlier versions (see the Decisions table).
 */
export interface Infographic {
  deckId: string;
  title: string;
  /** 3–6 sections, clamped on parse. */
  sections: InfographicSection[];
  /** Which cards this version was built from, kept for display only. */
  cardIds: string[];
  createdAt: number;
}

/**
 * What the model's response actually contains — title and sections only.
 * `Infographic` adds `deckId`, `cardIds` and `createdAt`, none of which are
 * in the model's own reply (it never sees a deck id, and doesn't need to:
 * `cardIds` is just which cards THIS caller happened to send it). Same
 * split `LlmCard` (cardPrompt.ts) already keeps from the stored `Flashcard`.
 */
export interface LlmInfographic {
  title: string;
  sections: InfographicSection[];
}
```

## Storage: `src/db/db.ts`

- `DB_VERSION` goes from `3` to `4`. The upgrade adds an `if (oldVersion < 4)` block that creates an `infographics` object store with `keyPath: 'deckId'`. The `oldVersion < 1/2/3` blocks do not change (same rule the folders migration already followed).
- New functions, one transaction each:
  - `getInfographic(deckId: string): Promise<Infographic | undefined>`
  - `saveInfographic(infographic: Infographic): Promise<void>` — a `put`, so generating again overwrites the existing row for that `deckId`.
- `deleteDeck` (`src/db/db.ts:266`) adds `'infographics'` to its transaction's store list and does one extra `tx.objectStore('infographics').delete(deckId)` alongside the existing `decks` delete — no cursor loop needed here (unlike `flashcards`/`testQuestions`), since it's one row per deck, addressed directly by key.

## Generation: prompt, transport, and the server

Follows the existing `cards` / `quiz` / `vignette` / `ocr` task pattern exactly — a new task name, `'infographic'`, touching the same handful of places those already do:

- **`src/lib/infographicPrompt.ts`** (new). Same shape as `quizPrompt.ts`: the system prompt text plus its response parser, nothing else, and — like every file in this family — **no runtime import of the DOM, `localStorage`, or anything else browser-only**, since the Netlify function imports it directly into the server bundle.
  - `INFOGRAPHIC_SYSTEM_PROMPT: string` — instructs the model: given some flashcards (front/back/context), write one infographic as JSON (`{ title, sections: [{ heading, icon, points }] }`), 3–6 sections, 2–5 points each, `icon` from the exact list of `InfographicIcon` values (spelled out in the prompt), headings and points short enough to read at a glance, no restating a card's back verbatim as a bullet — synthesize, don't transcribe.
  - `parseInfographicResponse(text: string, deckName: string): LlmInfographic | null` — the model replies with one JSON **object** (`{ title, sections }`), not the JSON array `parseJsonArray` (`textUtils.ts:214`) is built for, so this parser reuses only `stripJsonFence` (`textUtils.ts:147`, format-agnostic) and then does its own `{`…`}` slice + `JSON.parse`, the object-shaped equivalent of what `parseJsonArray` already does for arrays. Then **clamps rather than rejects**: more than 6 sections keeps the first 6; a section with more than 5 points keeps the first 5; an unrecognized `icon` value falls back to `'list'`; a missing/empty `title` falls back to `deckName` (since the model doesn't need to be told what it already isn't asked to invent). Returns `null` only when the response isn't parseable JSON at all or has zero usable sections — mirroring how `parseCardsResponse`/`parseQuizResponse` already treat a genuinely unusable response as "nothing," not a thrown error.
- **`src/lib/aiTransport.ts`** — add `'infographic'` to the `AiTask` union, `INFOGRAPHIC_SYSTEM_PROMPT` to the client-side `PROMPTS` map (used only in `byok` mode, which has no server to ask), and a `MAX_TOKENS.infographic` entry — a few thousand tokens is ample for this compact a JSON shape, well under `quiz`'s 8000.
- **`src/server/generateHandler.ts`** — the same two additions (`MAX_TOKENS`, `PROMPTS`), importing `INFOGRAPHIC_SYSTEM_PROMPT` from the same `src/lib/infographicPrompt.ts`, exactly as this file already does for the other four prompts — this is what keeps hosted and BYOK mode answering with the same shape, per the file's own header comment.
- **`src/lib/infographicGenerator.ts`** (new, mirrors `quizGenerator.ts`'s role, not its batching — this task is a single request, no retry batches): exports `generateInfographic(deckId: string, deckName: string, cards: Flashcard[], settings: AiSettings, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Infographic>`. Trims each card to `{ front, back, context }` the way `quizGenerator.ts` already trims cards before sending them, calls `callModel('infographic', payload, settings, signal)` (matching `callModel`'s real signature — `task, payload, settings, signal?, images?` — in `src/lib/aiTransport.ts:267`), parses the reply with `parseInfographicResponse(text, deckName)`, and assembles the full stored shape — `{ deckId, title: parsed.title, sections: parsed.sections, cardIds: cards.map(c => c.id), createdAt: Date.now() }` — throwing when parsing returned `null`, the same "failure the caller turns into a retryable notice" the existing generation flows already show. It does **not** call `saveInfographic` itself — `InfographicMode` does that after a successful call, keeping "generate" and "persist" as separate steps the way the rest of the app already does.

## UI/UX flow

- **`src/components/DeckManager.tsx`** gets one more button in `.manager-actions`, next to "Study this deck" / "Test this deck": **"Create infographic"**, `disabled={cards.length === 0}` (same guard the other two already use), calling a new `onInfographic(deckId)` prop.
- **`src/routes/router.tsx`** adds `{ path: 'deck/:deckId/infographic', element: <InfographicRoute /> }`.
- **`src/routes/DeckRoute.tsx`** wires `onInfographic={(id) => navigate(\`/deck/${id}/infographic\`)}`.
- **`src/routes/InfographicRoute.tsx`** (new) — reads `deckId` from the params, renders `InfographicMode`, wires `onExit={() => navigate('/')}` (matching Study/Test's own `onExit`; the top-bar's history-aware Back button, not this per-screen exit, is what already handles "return to wherever you came from" generically).
- **`src/components/InfographicMode.tsx`** (new) — the phase owner, `'setup' | 'generating' | 'view' | 'error'`, reading the deck's cards and any already-saved `Infographic` on mount (an existing one opens straight into `'view'`, so revisiting a deck doesn't lose last time's result):
  - **Setup** (`src/components/infographic/InfographicSetup.tsx`, new) — a choice between "All cards" (the default whenever Setup opens, including after a Regenerate) and "Choose cards"; choosing cards opens a checklist styled like the existing "+ Add decks" list (`DeckLibrary.tsx:409`, `.add-decks-list`) — one row per card, its front text as the label, a checkbox. Shows the same `AiSettingsPanel` gate `QuizSetup` already shows when `ai.mode === 'off'`. A "Generate infographic" button, disabled until at least one card is selected in "Choose cards" mode.
  - **Generating** — a simple loading state, matching `QuizGenerating`'s look.
  - **View** (`src/components/infographic/InfographicView.tsx`, new) — the title, then each section as a small card: icon, heading, bullet list. One layout, our own CSS, every deck's infographic looks like it belongs to the same app. A "Regenerate" button returns to Setup; the usual exit action matches Study/Test's.
  - **Error** — the same "here's what went wrong, try again" notice shape `QuizSetup`'s failed-generation state already uses.
- **`src/components/infographic/icons.tsx`** (new) — one small inline SVG per `InfographicIcon` value, in this app's existing icon style (24×24 viewBox, `stroke="currentColor"`, 2px stroke, round caps/joins — matching the delete/back-chevron icons already in the codebase).

No staleness tracking: unlike test questions (which compare a stored `cardHash` to detect an edited card), a saved infographic carries no signal that the cards it was built from have since changed — it simply reflects whatever they said at generation time, and Regenerate is how you get a fresh one. Worth calling out as a deliberate v1 cut, the same way export/download and version history are, rather than an oversight.

## What does not change

- Every other "Back to library" / exit control in the app (`StudyMode`, `QuizSetup`, the top bar) — untouched.
- No new AI mode, no new settings surface beyond the existing `AiSettingsPanel`.
- `getAllDecks()` / the library screen's read pattern — unaffected, since infographics live in their own store.

## Verification

- `parseInfographicResponse` is a pure function (no DOM, no network) — covered by a `tools/test-infographic.mjs` script in this repo's existing style (`tools/test-quiz.mjs` is the closest precedent: parser/clamping checks always run with no key; a second part that calls the real model only runs when one is set).
- The IndexedDB additions (`getInfographic`, `saveInfographic`, the `deleteDeck` cleanup, the v3→v4 upgrade) are checked the way this repo already checks browser-only storage code with no headless-browser runner available: manually, against the running dev server — the same category of check the back-navigation feature's own spec used for its browser-only behavior.
